pr_title: e2e: Wait for kube-root-ca.crt to be created
pr_body:
The change from service account secrets to projected tokens and the new dependency on kube-root-ca.crt to start pods with those projected tokens means that e2e tests can start before kube-root-ca.crt is created in a namespace. Wait for the default service account AND the kube-root-ca.crt configmap in normal e2e tests.

Also, it makes the wait for default service account secret EXPLICITLY check that it is the secret we expect, since anyone who automatically creates extra service account tokens in all namespaces could cause the wait to go too early.

We should have fixed this when we started adding kube-root-ca.crt, but a lot of these races are subtle flakes that don't pop up until long after or when we go log diving.

issue_context.title: e2e test should wait for kube-root-ca.crt to be created in the namespace
issue_context.body:
> I did a trivial pass on 1.20 -> 1.23 e2e serial runs in openshift ci environments, and while I see the failed mount errors during test pod creation, all of them seemed to be associated with races between the test creating the secret/config map and the pod getting created (i.e. some background controller creates the items, the kubelet gets the pod before the background controller can create the object).  These were serial jobs, so the kubelet is fairly lightly loaded.
> 
> Comparing to the parallel tests which run more hot (cpu is typically maxed on workers or close to it), I still don't see any obvious inexplicable FailedMount errors - instead I see the more explicable ones which are related to e2e tests apparently not waiting for kube-root-ca.crt to be created in the namespace.  I'll separate that out into a different issue since it's more of a noise in e2e (reducing my ability to spot true failures).  If we got a fix for that it would likely improve the ability to spot this in ci clusters.
> 
> So at least from a scan of CI runs, I don't see strong evidence of this being triggered by our e2e tests in dense clusters.  Which means that its frequency is low and/or the scenario that triggers it isn't exercised by the kube e2e suite.
> 
> Absent an obvious reproducer, I'll poke at the code next.

_Originally posted by @smarterclayton in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/105204#issuecomment-1021463140_

Pet peeve of mine: the `err` is a pretty uninformative "timed out waiting for the condition", so without an additional message, a failure is just:
```
Apr 21 13:00:31.563: FAIL: Unexpected error:
    <*errors.errorString | 0xc00042cd80>: {
        s: "timed out waiting for the condition",
    }
    timed out waiting for the condition
occurred
```

I know because I am hitting this in one of my downstream test scenarios... :sweat_smile: 

Please always add an explanation when calling ExpectNoError.
now that admission no longer uses this, we should drop the serviceAccountHasSecrets wait entirely
I need to check whether anyone depends on the token or has an explicit wait then.
Looks like no one explicitly tries to read the default token in core e2e.
